Evaluate the Yang et al. EPS kernel before support normalization.

Parameters
----------
dela : float or array_like
    Dimensionless linear-collapse barrier at the indicated epoch, extrapolated in the
    same growth convention.
s1 : float or array_like
    Dimensionless linear variance S=sigma**2 at the indicated host/subhalo/support mass.
    Active EPS terms require positive variance gaps.
s2 : float or array_like
    Dimensionless linear variance S=sigma**2 at the indicated host/subhalo/support mass.
    Active EPS terms require positive variance gaps.

Returns
-------
array_like
    delta_a/[sqrt(2*pi)*(s2-s1)**(3/2)], on positive variance support.

follow Yang et al., Eqs. (12)-(14), (21). Finite-gap normalization and zero-barrier
limits are numerical treatments of that kernel, not new empirical fits.

CDM-reference and SIDM views share accretion nodes and generation weights. Formation
before accretion is a domain requirement; invalid histories are not integrated backward
and carry zero survival weight. SIDM profile validity adds a separate mask to the shared
CDM tidal-truncation selection.

    zero-barrier-gap limit.

definitions.doc_after:
Run SIDM physical stages through the shared population executor.

Parameters
----------
M0 : float
    Reference host M200 in the variant internal mass unit. M0 normally refers to z=0;
    explicit epoch flags are described by the caller.
redshift : float or array_like
    Dimensionless redshift. The cosmological background requires z > -1; population
    nodes use nonnegative redshifts.
dz : float
    Positive nominal spacing of the accretion-redshift quadrature grid.
zmax : float
    Largest requested accretion redshift, above the target epoch; the actual grid
    convention belongs to this variant.
N_ma : int
    Number of logarithmically spaced accretion-mass nodes.
sigmalogc : float
    Nonnegative standard deviation of log10 concentration, in dex.
N_herm : int
    Positive Gauss-Hermite quadrature order for the scatter integrated by this routine:
    concentration in catalogue stages or host history in Na_calc.
logmamin : float, optional
    Lower or upper log10(M200_acc/Msun) bound. A None upper bound uses the model
    host-relative mass limit.
logmamax : float, optional
    Lower or upper log10(M200_acc/Msun) bound. A None upper bound uses the model
    host-relative mass limit.
N_hermNa : int
    Positive Gauss-Hermite order for the host-history scatter in the EPS accretion rate.
Na_model : {1, 2, 3}
    Yang EPS accretion/normalization prescription. This is a physical model selection,
    not a numerical tolerance.
ct_th : float
    Dimensionless tidal truncation threshold r_t/r_s; the specified strict survival rule
    is applied once through its mask.
M0_at_redshift : bool
    Interpret the input host mass at the target redshift and invert the prescribed
    history to obtain its z=0 reference value.
method : str
    picard (default), dop853, odeint, or an explicitly selected retained perturbative
    approximation.
**kwargs : dict
    Additional keyword options forwarded to the called routine; reserved scientific
    controls remain owned by that routine.

Returns
-------
dict[str, WeightedSubhaloCatalog]
    cdm_reference and sidm catalogues sharing aligned physical columns and independent
    generation factors, with distinct survival weights.

Notes
-----
The retained default scatter sigma(log10(c)) = 0.128 dex is the Ishiyama et al. Eq. (7),
Fig. 10 value for z=0 halos of 1e9 to 1e10 solar masses; Hiroshima et al. adopt the
rounded value 0.13 dex. Using one value across masses and redshifts is a model
assumption, not a quadrature error or a new calibration. The literature threshold rt/rs
> 0.77 follows the Hayashi et al. disruption prescription adopted by Hiroshima et al. A
caller-supplied threshold takes precedence in variants that expose it (C and SI
currently default to 0). This is a model selection rule; an exact-boundary test does not
calibrate disruption physics.

Masses are Msun, radii Mpc, densities Msun/Mpc^3 and named velocities km/s.
Formation-invalid SIDM entries remain explicitly zero and have zero survival weight. The
original arange(target+dz,zmax+dz,dz) grid convention is retained; non-aligned zmax may
be exceeded by less than one nominal step.

References
----------

.. [cite-scatter] Ishiyama et al. (2013), The Cosmogrid Simulation: Statistical Properties of Small Dark Matter Halos, Eq. (7), Fig. 10.
    https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.2020

.. [cite-structure] Hiroshima, Ando & Ishiyama (2018), Modeling evolution of dark matter substructure and annihilation boost, Section II, Eqs. (4)-(9), (28), (34).
    https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.07691

.. [cite-survival] Hayashi et al. (2003), The Structural Evolution of Substructure, Section 2.1.
    https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0203004

definitions.doc_after:
Returns the interpolation function of the effective cross section of SIDM divided by m.
The effective cross section is defined by Eq. (1.1) of Yang et al. (2023) [arXiv:2305.16176]:

$$
\sigma_{eff} = \frac{1}{512 \nu_{eff}^8} \int v^2 dv \int d\cos\theta \frac{d\sigma}{d\cos\theta} v^5 \sin^2\theta \exp(-v^2/4\nu_{eff}^2)
$$

where $\nu_{eff} = 0.64 V_{max}$ is a characteristic velocity dispersion of dark matter particles in the halo.

Parameters
----------
sigma0_m : float
    Cross section per mass; internal calls use Mpc**2/Msun. The result retains the supplied cross-section units.
w : float
    Characteristic speed in internal Mpc/s; convert a km/s value using self.km/self.s.

Returns
-------
sigma_eff_m_interpolate : scipy.interpolate.interp1d
    Interpolator from internal Vmax (Mpc/s) to cross section per mass in the supplied sigma0_m units; its velocity domain is 1e-5 to 1e3 km/s.

Notes
-----
The differential and viscosity cross sections are Yang & Yu, PDF Eqs. (2.1), (2.7).
Effective averaging uses nu_eff=0.64*Vmax and the 1/(512*nu_eff**8) normalization in
Yang et al., PDF Eq. (1.1). Finite velocity grids, the low-speed floor and asymptotic
switching thresholds are implementation controls.

definitions.doc_after:
Returns the analytic evaluation of the effective cross section of SIDM divided by m,
simplified via the substitution
    a = w^2/(4*nu_eff^2)   with   nu_eff = 0.64 * Vmax.

The expression is:

    sigma_eff = -sigma0_m * a^2 * [ exp(a) * (1+a) * Ei(-a) + 1 ]

where Ei(-a) is the exponential integral function.

For a > a_threshold, a degree-limited asymptotic expansion approaches
sigma0_m. For 20 <= a <= a_threshold, a positive integral evaluates the
same expression without subtractive cancellation.

Parameters
----------
sigma0_m : float
    Cross section per mass; internal calls use Mpc**2/Msun. The result retains the supplied cross-section units.
w : float
    Characteristic speed in internal Mpc/s; convert a km/s value using self.km/self.s.
a_threshold : float, optional
    The threshold for switching to the degree-limited asymptotic expansion.
    (Default is 703., based on that Ei(-a) returns NaN for such large a.)
degree : int, optional
    The degree of the polynomial expansion used for large a.
    (Default is 6, which gives a good approximation for large a.)
Returns
-------
sigma_eff : scipy.interpolate.interp1d
    Interpolator from internal Vmax to effective cross section per mass; its velocity domain is 1e-5 to 1e3 km/s.

Notes
-----
The differential and viscosity cross sections are Yang & Yu, PDF Eqs. (2.1), (2.7).
Effective averaging uses nu_eff=0.64*Vmax and the 1/(512*nu_eff**8) normalization in
Yang et al., PDF Eq. (1.1). Finite velocity grids, the low-speed floor and asymptotic
switching thresholds are implementation controls.

The exponential-integral closed form is derived by integrating the Rutherford cross
section in Yang et al. Eq. (1.1); the paper prints the defining integral, not this
closed form. With a=w**2/(4*nu_eff**2), the ratio is a**2*((1+a)*exp(a)*E1(a)-1). Its
positive-integral and asymptotic evaluations are numerical implementations of the same
derived expression.

The normalized D(z)=g(z)/[(1+z)*g(0)] and code redshift derivatives are derived uses. The DOI reaches a publisher landing page; the NED equation image provides accessible full text.

ludlow.title: Ludlow et al. (2016), The mass-concentration-redshift relation of cold and warm dark matter haloes, Appendix C.
ludlow.location: Eq. (3) and following text, p.5; Appendix C, pp.18-19, Eqs. (C8)-(C12)
ludlow.manual_comparison: The paper explicitly uses delta_sc(z)=1.686/D(z). The variance fit is sigma=22.26*xi^0.292/(1+1.53*xi^0.275+3.36*xi^0.198), xi=(M/(1e10 h^-1 Msun))^-1. It reports about 2.5% fit accuracy over 1e-7 to 1e15 h^-1 Msun. Differentiation is derived. WDM host histories integrate their spectrum and do not use this CDM variance fit; their redundant citation was removed.

correa.title: Correa et al. (2015), The accretion history of dark matter haloes - III. A physical model for the concentration-mass relation, Section 3 and Appendix B.
correa.location: Section 3, Eqs. (2)-(8), p.4; Appendix B, Eq. (B1), p.17
correa.manual_comparison: The anchored mass history, q=4.137*z_f^-0.9476 and z_f=-0.0064*log10(M)^2+0.0237*log10(M)+1.8837 are printed. Appendix B supplies both concentration-redshift branches and their coefficients. M is in physical Msun in these fits. History differentiation and combining a WDM spectrum with these coefficients are derived/adopted uses, not a WDM recalibration.

virial.title: Bryan & Norman (1998), Statistical Properties of X-ray Clusters: Analytic and Numerical Comparisons, Eq. (6).
virial.manual_comparison: For a flat matter-plus-Lambda cosmology the critical-density overdensity is 18*pi^2+82*x-39*x^2, x=Omega_m(z)-1. The paper reports roughly 1% fit accuracy for Omega_m(z)=0.1 to 1. This is distinct from a numerical solver tolerance and from an overdensity relative to mean matter.

conversion.title: Hu & Kravtsov (2003), Sample Variance Considerations for Cluster Surveys, Appendix C.
conversion.manual_comparison: The NFW mass-conversion approximation and inverse-fit coefficients are present. Eq. (C11) has a1=0.5116, a2=-0.4283, a3=-0.00313, a4=-3.52e-5, matching the code. The first value is 0.5116, not 1.5116. Root solving against the exact enclosed-mass identity is a separate derived conversion path.

nfw.title: Navarro, Frenk & White (1997), A Universal Density Profile from Hierarchical Clustering.
nfw.manual_comparison: The density and circular-speed laws are printed. f(x)=ln(1+x)-x/(1+x) follows by integrating the density. Potential with zero at infinity, exact mass-conversion root finding, and c=-1/W0(-exp[-(y+1)])-1 are derived consequences; the paper does not print the implementation's inverse or solver. The 2.163 and 4.625 factors are rounded maximum-speed identities.

tidal.title: Hiroshima, Ando & Ishiyama (2018), Modeling evolution of dark matter substructure and annihilation boost, Eqs. (23)-(24).

Reuse in other model backgrounds is an adopted prescription; solver agreement does not establish a new calibration.

Section II adopts scatter 0.13 dex; the disruption discussion and later selection factors use r_t/r_s=0.77. C/SI defaults allowing zero cutoff and all public 0.128-dex scatter defaults are explicit implementation choices, not literal copies of every population setting.
